report.source_text: Upon admission, laboratory tests showed: urinary protein 4+, red blood cells 71.9/uL, white blood cells 1.8/uL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; serum albumin 16.5 g/l; serum creatinine 63 µmol/L (corresponding to an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 123 mL/min/1.73 m² as calculated by the CKD-EPI equation); hemoglobin 115 g/L; white blood cell counts 3.68 × 10^9/L; mature lymphocyte counts 0.81 × 10^9/L; platelets were normal. CD4 + T cell counts: 77/Ul (reference range, 441–2156/uL); CD8 + T cell counts: 339/uL (reference range,125–1312/uL); CD4/CD8+: 0.23 (reference range, 0.71–2.78); NK cell counts 49/uL (reference range, 95–640/uL). TSH: 24.90 mIU/L, FT3: 3.44pmol/L, TT4: 53.80nmol/L, thyroglobulin: 52.40ng/Ml. Anti-nuclear antibody 1:100, anti-double-stranded DNA antibody with titer of 25.4/IU. All extractable nuclear antigen (ENA) test were negative. The complement C3 levels were reduced to 0.58 g/L, while complement C4 0.17 g/L was within the normal range. Subsequent investigations disclosed that the serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) concentration was markedly diminished, registering at 4.51 g/L. The assays for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA), anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) antibody, serum anti-M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) antibody, Coombs’test, antiphospholipid antibody, immunofixation electrophoresis, and tumor biomarkers all manifested negative findings. The viral serological screenings for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and rubella virus (RV) exhibited equivocal results. The diagnostic tests for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), syphilis, and HIV were all negative. Bone marrow flow cytometry analysis did not identify any conspicuous aberrant hematopoietic lymphocytes and plasma cells. Whole-genome sequencing failed to detect any genetic polymorphisms or mutations.

clinician.current_trajectory_hypothesis: 35-year-old Chinese male chef with 6-month foamuria and progressive generalized edema. Nephrotic-range proteinuria (4+ on urinalysis, 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g) with hematuria (RBC 71.9/uL) and preserved renal function (creatinine 63 µmol/L, eGFR 123 mL/min/1.73 m²). Additional findings include low serum albumin (16.5 g/L), low IgG (4.51 g/L), reduced C3 (0.58 g/L), elevated TSH (24.90 mIU/L), low-titer ANA (1:100) and anti-dsDNA (25.4 IU), negative ANCA/GBM/PLA2R antibodies, and normal bone marrow flow cytometry. The kidney biopsy findings would help characterize the etiology of proteinuria and its relationship to ICL.

report.source_text: Due to the development of visual field defects following hydroxychloroquine use(0.2 g orally twice daily), the patient discontinued the medication after less than two months of treatment. In light of the patient’s lack of efficacy in the hormonal treatment regimen and the exacerbation of verruca vulgaris following hormonal intervention, along with an immunocompromised state, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (SMZ) was prescribed prophylactically. We recommended immunoglobulin replacement to enhance immunity and mitigate the risk of infection; however, the patient declined due to financial concerns. Levothyroxine sodium (50 µg/day) was administered for subclinical hypothyroidism.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Chinese male chef presented with 6-month persistent foamuria and progressive generalized edema. Physical examination revealed severe pitting edema with mild verrucous hyperplasia on face and upper extremities, and severe coalescing verrucous lesions on lower extremities. Initial laboratory workup at another hospital showed CD4+ T-cell count of 30/μL. On admission, repeat testing confirmed severe CD4+ T-cell lymphocytopenia (CD4 77/μL, reference 441–2156/μL) with inverted CD4/CD8 ratio (0.23), low NK cells (49/μL), and low total lymphocytes (0.81 × 10^9/L). HIV serology and other infectious disease screening (hepatitis B/C, EBV, CMV, syphilis) were all negative, excluding HIV-related immunosuppression. Nephrotic-range proteinuria (4.5 g/24h) with hematuria was documented. Renal function was preserved (creatinine 63 µmol/L, eGFR 123 mL/min/1.73 m²). Kidney biopsy in November 2022 revealed secondary membranous nephropathy with class V lupus nephritis. Additional findings included markedly diminished IgG (4.51 g/L), reduced C3 (0.58 g/L), elevated TSH (24.90 mIU/L), low-titer ANA (1:100) and anti-dsDNA (25.4 IU), negative ANCA/GBM/PLA2R antibodies, and normal bone marrow flow cytometry. Whole-genome sequencing revealed no genetic mutations. Treatment included hydroxychloroquine (discontinued after <2 months due to visual field defects), prophylactic sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, and levothyroxine. Throughout the disease course, CD4+ T-cell count remained persistently below 150 cells/μL with no improvement despite prednisone taper to 7.5 mg/day and near-quiescent lupus activity. One-year follow-up was complicated by deep vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury, cytomegalovirus viremia, progressive verrucous lesions, and persistent proteinuria. The diagnosis of ICL was established based on the patient's persistent severe CD4+ T-cell lymphocytopenia, comprehensive medical history, clinical manifestations, entire treatment process, and results of various auxiliary examinations.
